title: Glutes, Quads, and Hamstrings Total Body Program
author: JP
desc:
This is an easy to follow, 3 day per week in the gym program designed to help you add shape, size, and athleticism to your lower body while still incorporating all muscle groups into the program. 

This program is great for beginners, novice, and intermediate lifters (advanced lifters would likely need to make some modifications). 

If you have struggled to add size to your glutes and legs, or work them out but are confused on what to do, but also dont want to ignore your upper body, this program is for you.  You will hit every major muscle group every workout with an emphasis on the legs.

ss.note: Starting weight should be around your 12 rep max (weight you can press 12 times maximum). When you can get that weight over 20-25 go  up in weight

ex.note: For treadmill alternate exercise, its walking on the treadmill at a high or max incline (ignore if you're doing stair master).
Aim for at least mid shin on depth.

ss.note: Full range of motion (go all the way down).
No bouncing and a full range of motion.
For the first 5 weeks of the program, no weight. Straight legs.

ex.note: Hold as long as you can, 1.5 minutes is a good starting point to aim for. Advanced athletes can hold from 2.5-3+ minutes

ss.note: Stay on bodyweight for first 5 weeks unless you are very experienced with the lift already. Use an adjustable bench and use same bench for incline dumbbell bench press
Use same bench as Bulgarian split squat bench, just adjust bench height to about 30 degrees high for dumbbell bench press.
Use a full range of motion, that means your toes are point up and heels down at the bottom of the rep and toes are down heels up at the top of the rep.

ex.note: Pause for at least 2 seconds on bottom for each rep.

ss.note: Take each set to failure. When you can't get to the top of the rep, don't stop the set, keep repping out small partial reps until the reps are almost nothing, then stop. Only count full reps for set
For the last set, do a two set drop set. Go to failure, drop the weight around 20% and go to failure, then drop it around another 20% and go to failure.

ex.note: 400 meters is 1 lap around a track or a quarter of a mile. Each set is 400 meters, or 1 lap around a track. Take a rest between each set. Use that rest to sprint not jog.
Same as a traditional RDL but go all the way to the ground and LIGHTLY tap the ground with the plates.

ss.note: Each rep is done "1 and a half" reps style. 1 rep= 1 and a half reps. Go down all the way, go up half way only, then go back down all the way, then go up all the way = 1 rep.
Add weight by pinching a 1, 2, or 5lb dumbbell between your feet. Optional: on all sets, drop the dumbbell once you reach failure and rep it out bodyweight until failure.

ex.note: Add weight by using a weighted vest or weight belt with weight attached to it. Start with light-moderate weight (15-35lbs). Keep same weight for a while and add time before increasing weight.

ss.note: Last set, drop the barbell and do bodyweight reps to failure on both legs.
Use same bench as Bulgarian split squat bench, just adjust bench height to about 30 degrees high for dumbbell bench press. Going heavier for this cycle.
Last set is a 2 drop-drop set. On the last set only, go to failure; wait 10 seconds and drop the weight approximately 20-30% and go to failure again. Repeat this one more time.
Use a full range of motion, that means your toes are point up and heels down at the bottom of the rep and toes are down heels up at the top of the rep.
